Container.Name: Orca
Container.Overview:
Always-on Orca headless server. Runs `orca-ide serve` (orcad) and serves the Orca web client on port 6768. The image is pulled from GHCR (ghcr.io/iilaurens/orca-unraid:latest).
Docker is the CLI only. It uses the standard /var/run/docker.sock, wired here to the separate `dind` container's socket file; this template does not mount the Unraid host Docker socket. Only the project tree is mounted here. dind keeps the tower's full /mnt mount, so per-workspace bind mounts under /mnt/user resolve through dind without giving Orca access to the rest of the array.
After the container starts, open the WebUI link to load the browser client. Then read the container log and paste the current `Pairing URL` into the web client. The pairing URL changes after a client pairs or when /config is reset, so read it from the log each time you add a browser.
Orca appdata, credentials, SSH keys, agent homes, and downloaded runtimes stay in /config. Pi's own home is /config/.pi, shared agent skills are /config/.agents/skills, and both are separate appdata mounts. Project checkouts belong under the mounted project tree, for example /mnt/user/development/my-repo.

Config.Name: Web UI
Config.Description: Orca web client and runtime websocket.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Orca profile, credentials, SSH keys, and runtime cache.

Config.Name: Pi home
Config.Description: Pi durable home: auth, settings, extension config, trust, model cache, and installed extensions.

Config.Name: Pi session dir
Config.Description: Container-layer path for Pi chat sessions. Lives and dies with the container; not persisted in appdata.

Config.Name: Agent skills
Config.Description: Global skills shared by Pi and other agent-skills harnesses.

Config.Name: Projects
Config.Description: Project checkouts Orca manages. Mount only the trees you use, not all of /mnt/user. Workspace bind mounts under /mnt/user are resolved by dind, which still mounts /mnt.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: Read-only bind mount of the Docker daemon socket. For dind use its socket file; for a normal host daemon use /var/run/docker.sock. Read-only prevents deleting or chmod-ing the socket; it does not restrict Docker API access.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: UID that owns files created in /config and the project tree. Unraid's nobody is 99.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: GID that owns files created in /config and the project tree. Unraid's users group is 100.

Config.Name: Docker socket GID
Config.Description: Group ID of the dind docker.sock. The dind template starts dockerd with --group users, so this is 100 unless you changed it.

Config.Name: Docker host (optional)
Config.Description: Leave empty to use /var/run/docker.sock. Set only for a TCP Docker daemon.

Config.Name: Orca port
Config.Description: Port orcad binds inside the container. Change the port mapping above in step.

Config.Name: Pairing address
Config.Description: Address clients use to reach Orca. Use a LAN hostname, LAN IP, or Tailscale IP that resolves from the client. Do not use 127.0.0.1 for another machine.

Config.Name: Extra serve flags
Config.Description: Optional space-separated extra flags passed to `orca-ide serve`, for example --mobile-pairing.

Config.Name: Shared orca-vm scripts
Config.Description: Location of the shared orca-vm lifecycle scripts inside the container. Change only if you mount them elsewhere.

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: File creation mask for new files.
